Convert an open_clip model to ONNX

Source: R/onnx.R
exportOnnxModel.Rd

Runs dimoose's export_onnx.py (in the package's python folder) to write a model as ONNX image and text encoders that onnxModel() runs without PyTorch. The conversion itself needs PyTorch and open_clip, but only once: the folder it writes can be copied to other computers or uploaded to a Hugging Face repository and used from there.

Usage

exportOnnxModel(
  name = "bioclip",
  pretrained = "openai",
  weights = NULL,
  dir = NULL,
  quantize = c("int8", "fp16"),
  python = NULL,
  run = NULL
)

Arguments

name

The model, as for visionModel(): an open_clip architecture name, "bioclip", "bioclip-2", "hf-hub:<organisation>/<model>" or "local-dir:<folder>". Only models with a vision transformer and open_clip's own CLIP tokenizer can be converted.

pretrained

open_clip's tag for the weights of an architecture.

weights

Local checkpoint file instead of a download.

dir

Folder to write to. By default the model's folder in onnxCache(), where onnxModel() and visionModel(backend = "onnx") find it by the same name.

quantize

Which smaller copies to write as well: "int8", "fp16", both or neither (character(0)).

python

The Python to run the script with; it needs the packages in the package's python/requirements.txt and python/requirements-export.txt. By default, if the uv program is installed, uv provides a Python with those packages (downloading them the first time); otherwise python3.

run

For tests: a function (command, args) that runs the script and returns its exit status.

Value

The folder, invisibly.

Details

Each file is checked against the PyTorch model as it is written; the script prints the files' sizes and how close their embeddings are.

Files written

  • dimoose_onnx.json: architecture, image size, patch size, embedding dimensions, preprocessing (resize, interpolation, crop, rescale, mean, std), the file names and sizes of each precision, and the names of the encoders' inputs and outputs.

  • image_encoder.onnx: input pixel_values (n x 3 x S x S, float32); outputs image_embeds (n x d, not normalised) and patch_embeds (n x g*g x d, the projected patch tokens).

  • text_encoder.onnx: input input_ids (n x 77, int64); output text_embeds (n x d, not normalised).

  • tokenizer.json: the tokenizer in the Hugging Face tokenizers format, which transformers.js also reads.

  • with quantize: image_encoder_int8.onnx, text_encoder_int8.onnx (weights as 8-bit integers, about a quarter of the size) and image_encoder_fp16.onnx, text_encoder_fp16.onnx (16-bit floats, half the size, same embeddings).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
exportOnnxModel("bioclip")
model <- onnxModel("bioclip", precision = "int8")
} # }
